_comment: Search profiles. Copy this file to profiles.json and describe your own
search; profiles.json is gitignored, because what you are looking for and
where you would move is yours rather than the repository's.
The three profiles below are unrelated on purpose: the file is a schema, not
a shortlist. `active` picks the default; JOBS_PROFILE overrides it per run.
Every value here is an illustration - replace them, do not inherit them.
roles / grades        searched as job title words on boards that search titles.
On AgileFluent they are closed lists the board does not
publish, matched exactly, and BOTH CUT SILENTLY - it
leaves role unset on about half its postings and grade
on a third, and those are dropped without a word. Leave
them empty to see the whole board; notes/agilefluent.md
has how to recover the values it does accept.
`grades` also becomes career.habr.com's qualification
filter, which knows intern, junior, middle, senior and
lead and answers anything else with zero results
relocationCountries   ISO-3166 alpha-3, used by the `countries` preset
skills                board tag slugs, PER BOARD. Vocabularies are not
portable: the same technology is spelled differently
on each board, an unknown slug returns zero results
rather than an error, and web3.career answers a slug
it does not have with a redirect to /404. Either a
plain list, used for every board, or a map keyed by
source - af, tm, w3, sol, hc, ats - with `default` for
the rest. A board with its own list does not also get
the default, which is what lets one board's slug sent
to another be refused here instead of failing mid-run.
What an entry MEANS is the board's own business: a tag
page slug on w3, a filter slug on tm, one free-text
search term on sol, a NUMERIC term id on hc
categories            names for board taxonomy ids, so a query reads
`category: "data"` instead of `38467`. The ids here
are TalentMove's; list them with
/wp-json/wp/v2/job_category?per_page=100&_fields=id,slug,name,count
Leave the map empty and pass raw ids until you have
looked yours up - a wrong id is a full answer from the
wrong filter, not an error
tagGroups             sets for the intersection filter. A board query can
only union tags, so an intersection is a second query
or a check on what came back. Each group is an OR,
because one idea is usually spread over several
interchangeable tags
watchlist             the employers the `ats` source follows: one entry per
company instance, `provider` one of greenhouse, ashby,
bamboohr, and `slug` that company's own instance name -
the subdomain or board path in the careers URL. `name`
is optional and only changes how the company is
labelled. Whose openings you follow is a shortlist, so
it lives here rather than in the repository, and the
slugs below are placeholders that will answer 404.
These links go to the employer's own application, which
is why applyAtEmployer is true for every record
signals               what to look for in a posting's own text, quoted back
in `note` and never acted on. Raised only where the
source publishes a description, which today is `ats`.
`phrases` maps a name you choose to the phrases that
raise it - the entry below is the sentence US employers
put on a posting that requires the right to work there.
`onsite` turns on office-presence detection, which
honours qualifiers: `hybrid` and `three days a week in
the office` raise it, `office optional` does not.
`languages` names the backend languages that disqualify
a posting FOR YOU - a language offered as an
alternative (`Go and/or Node.js`) does not raise it,
one stated as the requirement does. All three lists are
yours; the grammar around them is the repository's
